successors.note: Louis II died 30 January 1384 and his holdings passed to his daughter Margaret III, who ruled jointly with Philip the Bold. Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy shape 1385-1394 contains every cell of the 1384 Flanders shape; its row starts in 1385. The county itself, with its counts, lasted to 1795 inside the Burgundian and later Habsburg inheritance; the map follows Cliopatria in ending the Flemish colour in 1384.

region.text: the fief granted to Baldwin I

ledger.note: 862: Baldwin I becomes the first Count of Flanders. Infobox: 'Fief granted to Count Baldwin I in 862'; the text: he 'became count in 862 after he eloped with Judith of West Francia'. The page gives the year, not the boundary.
898: Baldwin II integrates Artois into Flanders. The Artois page: Baldwin II 'integrated Artois into Flanders from 898'. It does not say from whom; West Francia is the overlord of the time.

region.text: Valenciennes on the right bank of the Scheldt

ledger.note: 1013: Baldwin IV receives Valenciennes. The Baldwin IV page: he 'received Valenciennes (1013)' on the right bank of the Scheldt; it also says Emperor Henry II gave him Zeeland as a fief, with no year, so Zeeland is not drawn. Counterpart is the Empire because Valenciennes lies east of the Scheldt (the Flanders page: Imperial Flanders held as an Empire fief from the 11th century).

1167: Philip of Alsace and Elisabeth inherit Vermandois. The Philip I page: 'In 1156, Philip married Elisabeth, elder daughter of count Ralph I of Vermandois' and after Ralph II abdicated in 1167 'Elisabeth and Philip inherited the County of Vermandois'. The page does not mention Valois or Amiens.

1185: the Treaty of Boves gives the king Amiens and Montdidier. Crown lands page: Philip II 'gains Amiens and Montdidier' and rights 'to the inheritance of Vermandois and Valois' by the 1185 Treaty of Boves. The page does not say the lands were Flemish; that they were rests on the Cliopatria 1169 shape (it holds Amiens) and on the Philip I page (Vermandois). The Treaty of Boves page itself did not load.

1186: Philip cedes Vermandois to the king. 'a peace treaty with King Philip II and Count Baldwin V on 10 March 1186, recognizing the cession of Vermandois to the king'; the page adds Philip kept the title of Count of Vermandois for life. The Crown lands page dates the king's acquisition of Vermandois 1191 ('the County of Vermandois is acquired by the king' after Elisabeth's death) and the Kingdom of France dossier agrees; Cliopatria's Flemish shape loses these cells in 1188. Reviewer eu-10-b: confidence lowered to 2 because the County of Vermandois page says 'the count of Flanders kept the county of Vermandois until his death, in 1191' (the 1186 treaty recognised the cession; the land moved in 1191).

1191: Artois leaves Flanders. The Flanders page: Artois 'Removed in 1191 and made an independent county in 1237'. Background from the Artois page: Philip of Alsace gave Artois as dowry to Isabelle of Hainaut at her marriage to Philip II (infobox 'To France as dowry: 28 April 1180'); after her death in 1190 the French crown claimed it as a reverted fief against strong Flemish opposition; Louis VIII took Count Ferrand at Bouvines in 1214 and the Treaty of Melun (1226) confirmed it. Philip died at Acre on 1 August 1191 (Philip I page). Cliopatria drops Artois in 1188.
1264: Guy of Dampierre becomes Marquis of Namur. The Guy page gives 'Marquis of Namur (1264-1305)'; it does not say how he obtained the title.

1297: Philip IV invades Flanders. 'The army reached the border near Douai on 14 June and entered Flanders on 16 June'; Lille was besieged from 17 June and surrendered after the French won at Furnes (20 August). After the January 1300 invasion 'the whole of Flanders was under French control' (Ghent 8 May, Ypres 21 May 1300); the Bruges Matins (19 May 1302) and the Golden Spurs (11 July 1302) restored Flemish control; the French won at Mons-en-Pévèle (18 August 1304).
1305: Namur leaves the count of Flanders. The Guy page ends 'Marquis of Namur' at 1305, the year Guy died (7 March 1305, in prison at Compiegne). The page does not say who took Namur.

region.text: Lille, Douai and Orchies, the Romance (Walloon) Flanders

ledger.note: 1305: Lille, Douai and Orchies pass to the French crown. The Franco-Flemish War page: the Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge (23 June 1305) 'recognised Flemish independence as a fief' and 'Lille, Douai, and Béthune' were 'transferred to the French crown-lands'. The page is silent on Orchies (named in the Louis II page as part of Romance Flanders, which came back in 1369) and on the Treaty of Pontoise of 1312.
1305: the Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge ends the Franco-Flemish War; Flanders keeps its independence 'as a fief of the French kingdom' and pays large fines.

1322: Louis I unites Nevers with Flanders. 'succeeded his father as count of Nevers and his grandfather as count of Flanders in 1322'; Robert III died 17 September 1322 (Robert III page). Personal union: Nevers keeps its own dossier.

region.text: Rethel, the county of Joan, mother of Louis I

ledger.note: 1326: Rethel enters the Flemish shape. Page silent on the year: the Louis I page names his mother 'Joan, Countess of Rethel' without a date and the Louis II page gives 'Count of Flanders, Nevers, and Rethel' for 1346-1384; the year and the land rest on the Cliopatria 1326 shape. Rethel needs a gazetteer name and a dossier.

region.text: Antwerp and Mechelen, held under the Peace of Ath of 4 June 1357

ledger.note: 1357: the Peace of Ath gives Louis II Antwerp and Mechelen. The Louis II page: he invaded Brabant and captured Brussels in August 1356; at the Peace of Ath (4 June 1357) he kept the title of Duke of Brabant for life and reclaimed Mechelen and gained Antwerp for the county. The page does not say when they were lost; Cliopatria never draws them.

region.text: Lille, Douai and Orchies, the Romance (Walloon) Flanders

ledger.note: 1369: Romance Flanders returns. Louis arranged the marriage of Margaret to Philip the Bold in exchange for 'the return of Romance Flanders' (Lille, Douai, Orchies), 19 June 1369.

1384: Flanders passes to the Dukes of Burgundy. Louis II died 30 January 1384 and his holdings 'were passed onto his surviving daughter, Margaret III', who ruled jointly with Philip the Bold; the Flanders page: 'From 1384, the county was politically united to the Duchy of Burgundy'.
1384: the county's own line ends. The Flanders page: the county was united to the Duchy of Burgundy from 1384 and annexed by France in 1795; the map ends the Flemish colour here.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Flanders and Hainault
wars.outcome: Guy's side lost at Walcheren in 1253 and Guy was taken prisoner; by the mediation of Louis IX he was ransomed in 1256. The page gives no border change.
wars.note: The page does not date the start of the war; 1253 is the first year it gives.

wars.name: Franco-Flemish War

zones.text: Flanders, under French control from May 1300 to 1302
Lille, Douai and Orchies, the Romance (Walloon) Flanders

wars.outcome: French victory at Furnes (1297) and conquest of Flanders (1300); Flemish victory at the Golden Spurs (11 July 1302); French victory at Mons-en-Pévèle (1304). Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge, 23 June 1305: Flemish independence as a fief, Lille, Douai and Béthune to the French crown.
wars.note: Guy renounced his vassalage in January 1297 and allied with Edward I of England (Guy page also gives 1297). Guy died in French captivity on 7 March 1305.

wars.name: Flemish revolt of 1323-1328
wars.outcome: Tax unrest became an uprising in 1323 led by Nicolaas Zannekin; the rebels took Nieuwpoort, Veurne, Ypres and Kortrijk and captured Louis; Charles IV intervened and the Peace of Arques was sealed on 26 April 1326; the rebels were defeated by the French royal army at Cassel in 1328. No border changed.

wars.name: Uprising of Jacob van Artevelde at Ghent
wars.outcome: Edward III's wool boycott helped spark a 1337 uprising under Artevelde; Louis I fled his lands in 1339 and never returned. No border changed.
wars.note: The page gives only 1337 and 1339; the end of the rising is not dated.

wars.name: Louis II's invasion of Brabant

zones.text: Antwerp and Mechelen, held under the Peace of Ath of 4 June 1357

wars.outcome: Louis captured Brussels in August 1356 and seized the duchy; at the Peace of Ath (4 June 1357) he kept the Brabant title for life and reclaimed Mechelen and gained Antwerp for the county.

wars.name: Ghent revolt (White Hoods)
wars.outcome: The revolt broke out in 1379 and continued beyond Louis of Male's death on 30 January 1384. No border changed.
wars.note: The end year of the revolt is not on the page; 1384 is the count's death.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines in the pages opened; the Imperial and royal fiefs overlap east and west of the Scheldt.
The Lille-Douai-Orchies line is fixed by the treaty of 23 June 1305 and the 1369 return, and the Peace of Ath (4 June 1357) fixes the Antwerp-Mechelen holdings; every other frontier stays soft.

notes: Not settled. (1) Dossier start is 862 (Flanders page infobox); the Cliopatria row starts 990, so 862-989 are two new keyframes (core, then core plus Artois from 898). West Francia is the west-franks dossier. (2) Cliopatria draws Bruges (the capital), and the coast from Bruges to Zeelandic Flanders, outside the 1010-1259 shapes; every shape in that span has an adjust that adds a 25 km radius around Bruges. (3) The 1272-1304 and 1326-1384 shapes carry a 54-cell Nevers block. Before 1322 it was held by Robert III (Count of Nevers by marriage) and his son Louis, not by the Count of Flanders, so it is removed for 1272-1304; from 1322 Nevers is in personal union with Flanders (Louis I page). Nevers has its own row 1285-1325 and none for 1326-1406. (4) Rethel enters the shape in 1326 on no page: confidence 1; Rethel needs a dossier. (5) Cliopatria keeps Lille, Douai and Orchies in every Flemish shape after 1305; the Franco-Flemish War page says Lille, Douai and Béthune went to the French crown in 1305 and the Louis II page says Romance Flanders returned in 1369. The Treaty of Pontoise (1312) and the 1320 settlement were not on any page opened. (6) The Mons cells (Hainaut) in the 1260-1304 shape and the ten Cambrai-Douai-Valenciennes cells of 1169-1187 are explained by no page opened; the Guy page does not mention Hainaut as his land. (7) Zeeland west of the Scheldt, given as a fief by Henry II (Baldwin IV page, undated), is not drawn. Antwerp and Mechelen (1357) are not in any Cliopatria shape; they are added by the 1357-1384 keyframes. (8) The page of the Treaty of Boves (1185) did not load (url_not_found); the Crown lands page gives Amiens and Montdidier to the king by it. The dates of the French acquisition of Vermandois differ: 10 March 1186 (Philip I page) against 1191 (France dossier, Crown lands page). (9) No full list of counts was on the pages opened, so identity.rulers is left out; the counts met on the pages are Baldwin IV (988-1035), Philip of Alsace (1168-1191), Guy of Dampierre (to 1305), Robert III (1305-1322), Louis I (1322-1346), Louis II (1346-1384). (10) Gazetteer names needed: Valenciennes, Douai, Orchies, Mechelen (places); Nevers block and Rethel as regions. Counterparts needing dossiers: county-of-namur, county-of-rethel, county-of-hainaut.
